facts.statement: Similicaudipteryx is a genus of theropod dinosaur belonging to the family Caudipteridae.
facts.quote: Similicaudipteryx, meaning "similar to Caudipteryx" (which itself means "tail feather"), is a genus of theropod dinosaur of the family Caudipteridae.

facts.statement: The genus Similicaudipteryx was named and described in 2008 by He Tao, Wang Xiaolin, and Zhou Zonghe.
facts.quote: In 2008 the new genus Similicaudipteryx, with as type species Similicaudipteryx yixianensis, was named and described by He Tao, Wang Xiaolin and Zhou Zonghe.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in the Jiufotang Formation of northeastern China and dates to approximately 120 million years ago, or possibly 112 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, IVPP V 12556, was recovered from the Jiufotang Formation of northeastern China, dating to the early Cretaceous Period middle Aptian stage, about 120 million years ago or perhaps early Albian stage, about 112 million years old.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a nearly complete adult skeleton that lacks the skull, front neck, and hands.
facts.quote: It consists of a nearly complete skeleton of an adult individual compressed on a plate, that however lacks the skull, the front neck and the hands.

facts.statement: In 2010, two additional juvenile specimens with feather preservation were referred to Similicaudipteryx, but have since been re-interpreted as belonging to Incisivosaurus gauthieri.
facts.quote: In 2010, two additional specimens with extensive feather preservation were referred to Similicaudipteryx, one of a juvenile, STM4-1, and the other of a much larger juvenile, STM22-6.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of Similicaudipteryx at one meter and its weight at seven kilograms in 2010.
facts.quote: Paul in 2010 estimated the length at one metre, the weight at seven kilogrammes.

facts.statement: Similicaudipteryx possessed a unique dagger-shaped pygostyle made of the two most extreme tail vertebrae, a feature not found in its relatives.
facts.quote: Similicaudipteryx also differed from its relatives by possessing a dagger-shaped pygostyle (the bone at the end of the tail to which feathers anchor in birds) consisting of the two most extreme tail vertebrae and several unique features of the back vertebrae.

facts.statement: Similicaudipteryx had an exceptionally long pubic bone relative to the ilium.
facts.quote: The pubic bone was exceptionally long relative to the ilium.

facts.statement: Although the holotype lacks feather traces, researchers speculate feathers were present because the pygostyle serves as an anchor point for tail feathers in modern birds.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen lacks traces of feathers, but He and colleagues speculated that they were probably present based on its pygostyle, the anchor point of long tail feathers (rectrices) in modern birds.

facts.statement: Similicaudipteryx lived during the middle Cretaceous Period, approximately 124 to 120 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 124 y 120 millones de años, en el Aptiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The describers assigned Similicaudipteryx to the family Caudipteridae without performing an exact cladistic analysis of its position.
facts.quote: Similicaudipteryx fue asignado por sus descriptores a los Caudipteridae . No se realizó un análisis cladístico exacto de su posición.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul renamed the species Caudipteryx yixianensis, but this change has not been accepted by the scientific community.
facts.quote: En 2010, Gregory S. Paul cambió el nombre de la especie a Caudipteryx yixianensis, pero esto no ha encontrado aceptación.

facts.statement: Like Caudipteryx, Similicaudipteryx had a short snout with a lower jaw curved downward.
facts.quote: Como Caudipteryx, tenía un hocico corto con una mandíbula inferior curvada hacia abajo.

facts.statement: Similicaudipteryx had relatively short arms and long legs.
facts.quote: Tenía brazos relativamente cortos y piernas largas.

facts.statement: A cladistic analysis by Lamanna et al. placed Similicaudipteryx within the family Caudipteridae.
facts.quote: En la descripción de Anzu wyliei, miembro de la familia Caenagnathoidea, Lamanna et al. realizaron un análisis cladistico con su posterior cladograma colocando Similcaudipteryx dentro Caudipteridae.

facts.statement: The time range for Similicaudipteryx is estimated to be between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
